title: The Silent Archive
overview: A rare first-edition manuscript vanishes from a university archive with no sign of forced entry. A scheduled catalog migration provides a convenient explanation.
objective: Establish whether the manuscript was misplaced during routine cataloging or removed by someone who understood the archive's procedures.

hypotheses.statement: Archivist Simone Vale used a planned catalog move to remove the manuscript and falsify its location.
The manuscript was misplaced during the scheduled catalog migration.

evidence.title: Collection discrepancy report
evidence.content: A first-edition manuscript is missing from a sealed archive room. The catalog lists it as temporarily relocated during migration.

evidence.title: Archive staff and access roles
evidence.content: Simone Vale supervised cataloging; assistant Noor Patel and conservator Emil Hart had escorted access.

evidence.title: Catalog change history
evidence.content: The relocation entry was created three days before the migration began using Simone Vale's administrator account. No move ticket or destination shelf was recorded.

evidence.title: Reading room access log
evidence.content: Simone Vale entered the archive alone after closing on the evening the catalog entry was created. The migration team had not yet received access.

evidence.title: Conservation bench inventory
evidence.content: A custom acid-free transport sleeve issued to Simone was missing from the conservation bench, but no relocation was logged.

suspects.name: Simone Vale
suspects.role: Senior archivist with catalog administrator access

witness_statements.statement: The migration had not started when the manuscript relocation entry was added.

timeline.event: A relocation entry was created without a destination or move ticket.
Simone Vale entered the archive alone.
A transport sleeve issued to Simone was found missing.
